notes:
Lead: SparkDock builds a lightweight helpdesk + automation for small e-commerce merchants.
Primary ask: hosted API (self-serve) to power ticket summarization + structured output mapping into Zendesk fields and tool-calling to query Shopify order status.
Key quotes: "Need crisp 3–5 line summaries for merchants and a JSON payload we can map 1:1 to ticket fields" — Lila (CEO).
Cost: very price-sensitive; volume = 1k–3k tickets/month initially, expect seasonal spikes. Wants auto-fallback to cheaper model for nightly batch summaries.
Latency/throughput: agent-assist path needs ~<300ms median for interactive summaries in agent UI; background batch summarization can be relaxed to <2s/token.
Model preference: open to Redwood-curated small/medium models if quality meets prompt tests; wants recommendation for quantized faster models for batch.
Security: require SSO/SAML for console access, audit logs for API keys, and a basic data residency option (NA) + retention controls. Not yet asking for on-prem.
Tech notes: Will use function/tool-calling to run two lookups before summary: order status + refund history. Needs structured JSON with exact keys: {ticket_summary, priority, order_id, recommended_action}. (we provided sample schema but they will validate).
Current mood: positive — likes self-serve flow. Biggest risk: cost vs accuracy tradeoff on small model variants.
Ask: Redwood to provide short-run benchmark on their ticket dataset (5–10 sample tickets) and a cost estimate for interactive vs batch modes.
use_case_summary: Inbound SMB focused on hosted API self-serve. Workload = ticket summarization (interactive + nightly batch), structured JSON output for direct Zendesk mapping, and tool-calling for Shopify/order lookups. Latency SLA: interactive ~300ms median; batch relaxed. Cost sensitivity high; prefer fallback routing to cheaper model for high-volume tasks. Security: SSO/SAML + audit logs + NA residency.
